narr: A warm front, drifting northward from the Carolinas across the lower Mid-Atlantic, triggered scattered thunderstorms with heavy rain. Strong heating during the afternoon supported surface-based CAPE values rising into the 2,000 to 2,500 J/Kg range, while precipitable water values ranged from around 1.5 inches along the Blue Ridge to in excess of 1.8 inches across the central Piedmont of Virginia and North Carolina. Wind speeds through 700 mb were generally around 10 knots, supporting slow cell movement that would contribute to prolonged heavy rainfall over some locations. Many of the storms produced rainfall at 3 to 5 inch per hour rates, which resulted in flash flooding of small streams in the local area.
ev: Heavy rain caused a tributary of Mill Creek to overflow its banks and flood across Old Chapel Road near the intersection with Kennel Hill Lane. The road was reopened after flooding receded, with no damage reported.
Heavy rain caused Marlbrook Creek to overflow its banks and flood across Sterrett Road. The road was reopened after flooding receded, with no damage reported.
Blacks Run was flooded by up to 3 feet of water flowing across the roadway due to heavy rain. The road was reopened after flood water receded and no damage was reported.

A passing thunderstorm produced rainfall rates ranging from 4 to 5 inches per hour, which inundated Powder Mill Creek. The creek was observed flowing over 6 inches deep across School Board Road, making the road impassible. The road reopened after flood waters receded, with no damage reported.

Campbell Branch was observed overflowing its banks and flooding several inches deep across Commerce Street near the town of Stuart. No damage was reported and the road was open after the flooding receded.

Three to four inches of rain from a slow moving thunderstorm caused several roads within the Hillsville area to become flooded and impassible. Some of the roads were flooded 1 to 2 feet deep where they intersected small flooded streams. Some of the streams overflowed their banks across U.S. Highway 52, making the highway impassible at some locations. The roads were passible again once the flooding receded, with no damage reported.

Lovills Creek was observed overflowing its banks and flooding several inches deep across Wards Gap Road. The road was impassible until the flood waters receded. No damage was reported to the road and it was reopened after flooding ended.

Three to four inches of rain fell along the crest of the Blue Ridge between the communities of Fancy Gap and Meadows of Dan, resulting in flooding of several small streams along the Blue Ridge Parkway. Some of these streams flooded across the parkway several inches deep, making the road impassible until the flood waters receded. No damage was reported. CREST (Coupled Routing and Excess Storage) Unit Streamflow estimated as much as 600 cfs per mi^2 in this area.
Little Spoon Creek was observed overflowing its banks and flooding several inches deep across Highway 58. The highway was reopened after flooding receded and no damage was reported.
